legend: Given a natural number n%%ZSMJ0%%, count the number of permutations (p1,p2,…,pn)%%ZSMJ1%% of the numbers from 1%%ZSMJ2%% to n%%ZSMJ3%%, such that for each i%%ZSMJ4%% (1≤i≤n%%ZSMJ5%%), the following property holds: pi mod pi+1≤2%%ZSMJ6%%, where pn+1=p1%%ZSMJ7%%.
As this number can be very big, output it modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ8%%.
input: The only line of the input contains the integer n%%ZSMJ9%% (1≤n≤106%%ZSMJ10%%).
output: Output a single integer — the number of the permutations satisfying the condition from the statement, modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ11%%.
note: For example, for n=4%%ZSMJ12%% you should count the permutation [4,2,3,1]%%ZSMJ13%%, as 4 mod 2=0≤2%%ZSMJ14%%, 2 mod 3=2≤2%%ZSMJ15%%, 3 mod 1=0≤2%%ZSMJ16%%, 1 mod 4=1≤2%%ZSMJ17%%. However, you shouldn't count the permutation [3,4,1,2]%%ZSMJ18%%, as 3 mod 4=3>2%%ZSMJ19%% which violates the condition from the statement.
